_note: The size guide: frostlinenorge.no/storrelser and the Storrelser button on each garment page (build.py size_guide).
All numbers are cm with the garment lying flat, so a width is half the way round.
Zip hoodie, hoodie, crewneck, bukse and shorts: measured by hand on stock garments, unwashed, along the lines drawn here (2026-10-06),
single pieces evened out where one size jumped against its neighbours. The three tops are one block at the factory, so they share one set,
taken from the crewneck (the hoodie's own chest read 7-9 cm under in every size, which a lab test of the same hoodie contradicts).
Where a measurement came out within about 1 cm of the factory spec (Qianshi ERP 2026-06-24, 2026-china-size-charts.xlsx in
~/ftmerch-print-workspace/stock/suppliers/china-qianshi/size-charts) the spec stayed: men's waist, inseam and leg opening, shorts waist,
women's shorts leg opening. Women's pants gained XXL (measured; the factory sheet stops at XL). The ERP calls its numbers after wash;
the stock measured shorter than that before washing, so these are the garment as it arrives.
Bukse herre and dame inseam: as measured plus 2 cm, the length the 2026-10 bulk is ordered with (Alexander, 2026-10-06).
The pants and the hoodie have ribbed side panels, and the hand measurements went rib to rib, leaving them out: so the hoodie chest
comes from the crewneck, and the pants' hip (both cuts) and the women's leg opening stay at the factory spec; the women's XXL
carries the spec's own step on from XL (hip +2.5, leg opening +1).
Women's shorts leg opening is the one girth the factory gives the whole way round; halved here, to one decimal.
T-skjorte, longsleeve and singlet: the russ print guide, ~/ftmerch-print-workspace/size-guide/storrelsesguide.html (KILDER.md there),
which is the size a group orders, not the blank: a t-shirt or singlet ordered in M is an S blank (SOURCE_SIZE_OFFSET in
src/lib/stock/pools.js), and the singlet starts at S because an ordered XS would need a blank that is not made. If that offset table
changes, these three tables are wrong the same day.
Collegejakke has no table: the factory promised one in July 2026 and never sent it.
mark: the measuring line on the product photo (img/shop/-1200.webp), points in that 1200 x 1200 picture, read off the
cut-out's outline; two points are a straight line, three bend at the middle one (a sleeve over the shoulder). at: where along
the line its letter sits (default the middle of the longest stretch), to keep it off the other lines.
A garment with two cuts (bukse, shorts) shows both side by side in one table, so a letter must mean the same
measurement in both cuts (build.py stops if not); a measurement only one cut has goes last (women's shorts' hip, D).
